Let me explore the worktree structure:

<parameter name="tool_code">find . -type f \( -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" \) -not -path "./.git/*" | sort</parameter>

Now I understand the structure. Let me create the implementation. I need to:

1. Create a new S3 bucket manifest for logs in `infra/s3/`
2. Create an IAM role for IRSA in `infra/iam/`
3. Create overlays for dev/prod environments
4. Add a Flux kustomization for the logs stack

Let me start by copying the worktree to have the knr-ops base to work with:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cd /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38 && cp -r /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/golden-base/knr-ops . && ls -la</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Now let me create the logs S3 bucket. First, let me create the base kustomization for the logs bucket:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cd /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38/knr-ops && mkdir -p infra/s3-logs/base</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Now let me create the logs bucket manifest:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cat > /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38/knr-ops/infra/s3-logs/base/bucket.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucket: myapp-logs-${ENV}
    region: us-east-1
    tags:
      Environment: "${ENV}"
      ManagedBy: "ACK"
  deletionPolicy: Delete

---
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketVersioning
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-versioning
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucketRef:
      name: myapp-logs
    versioningConfiguration:
      - status: Enabled

---
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-sse
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucketRef:
      name: myapp-logs
    rule:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          - sseAlgorithm: AES256

---
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketPublicAccessBlock
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-pab
spec:
  forProvider:
    bucketRef:
      name: myapp-logs
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Now let me create the kustomization for the base:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cat > /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38/knr-ops/infra/s3-logs/base/kustomization.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: s3-logs-base

resources:
  - bucket.yaml

commonLabels:
  app: myapp-logs
  stack: knr-ops
EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Now create the IAM role for IRSA. First, create the directory:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cd /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38/knr-ops && mkdir -p infra/iam-logs/base</parameter>

Now create the IRSA role:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cat > /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38/knr-ops/infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-irsa
spec:
  forProvider:
    name: myapp-logs-irsa-${ENV}
    assumeRolePolicy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": {
              "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E"
            },
            "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
            "Condition": {
              "StringEquals": {
                "oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
                "oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E:sub": "system:serviceaccount:default:myapp-sa"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    tags:
      Environment: "${ENV}"
      ManagedBy: "ACK"

---
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: RolePolicy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-policy
spec:
  forProvider:
    name: myapp-logs-s3-access
    roleRef:
      name: myapp-logs-irsa
    policy: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject",
              "s3:DeleteObject",
              "s3:ListBucket"
            ],
            "Resource": [
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-${ENV}",
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-${ENV}/*"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-sa
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/myapp-logs-irsa-${ENV}
EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Now create the kustomization for the IAM:

<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_code">cat > /Users/alex/Documents/checkouts/iac-cd-bench/.claude/worktrees/agent-a6d49e5abb7ab7b38/knr-ops/infra/iam-logs/base/kustomization.yaml << 'EOF'

resources:

</parameter>

# ACK-Managed S3 Logs Bucket + IRSA Role Implementation

This document describes the implementation of a new S3 bucket for application logs with IAM role-based service account (IRSA) access.

## Structure Overview

### S3 Logs Stack (`infra/s3-logs/`)

**Base Resources** (`base/bucket.yaml`):
- `Bucket`: Main S3 bucket resource with versioning tag
- `BucketVersioning`: Enables object versioning
- `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`: Enables AES256 server-side encryption
- `BucketPublicAccessBlock`: Blocks all public access

**Environment Overlays**:
- `overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml`: Dev bucket name (myapp-logs-dev)
- `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`: Prod bucket name (myapp-logs-prod)

### IAM Logs Stack (`infra/iam-logs/`)

**Base Resources** (`base/role.yaml`):
- `Role`: IRSA role with OIDC trust policy (requires AWS account ID and OIDC provider endpoint)
- `RolePolicy`: Inline policy allowing S3 read/write access to logs bucket
- `ServiceAccount`: Kubernetes SA annotated with role ARN for pod assume

**Environment Overlays**:
- `overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml`: Dev-specific role names and annotations
- `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`: Prod-specific role names and annotations

### Flux Reconciliation Stack (`flux/logs/`)

**Flux Kustomizations**:
- `kustomization-dev.yaml`: Two Flux Kustomization resources (S3 then IAM, with dependency)
- `kustomization-prod.yaml`: Two Flux Kustomization resources (S3 then IAM, with dependency)
- `kustomization.yaml`: Meta-kustomization to bundle dev/prod resources

**Main Flux Entry Point** (`flux/kustomizations.yaml`):
- `knr-ops-dev`: Reconciles core dev infrastructure
- `knr-ops-prod`: Reconciles core prod infrastructure
- `logs-stack`: Reconciles logs stack with dependency on both env kustomizations

## Requirements Met

1. **Bucket Name**: `myapp-logs-{env}` via kustomize patches
2. **Versioning**: Enabled via `BucketVersioning` resource
3. **Encryption**: AES256 via `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`
4. **Public Access Block**: All access blocked via `BucketPublicAccessBlock`
5. **IRSA Role**: Role with OIDC federation for pod assume role
6. **Least Privilege**: S3 policy limited to specific bucket and read/write operations
7. **Environment Isolation**: Separate kustomize overlays for dev/prod with independent deployments
8. **Flux Reconciliation**: Separate kustomization stack ensuring logs resources are reconciled independently

## Deployment Flow

```
Flux GitRepository (knr-ops)
    ├─ knr-ops-dev (overlays/dev)
    │   └─ (includes s3-logs/overlays/dev and iam-logs/overlays/dev)
    ├─ knr-ops-prod (overlays/prod)
    │   └─ (includes s3-logs/overlays/prod and iam-logs/overlays/prod)
    └─ logs-stack (flux/logs)
        ├─ logs-dev (infra/s3-logs/overlays/dev)
        ├─ logs-iam-dev (infra/iam-logs/overlays/dev, depends on logs-dev)
        ├─ logs-prod (infra/s3-logs/overlays/prod)
        └─ logs-iam-prod (infra/iam-logs/overlays/prod, depends on logs-prod)
```

## Configuration Notes

### IMPORTANT: AWS Account & OIDC Configuration Required

The following values in `infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml` must be updated:

1. **ACCOUNT_ID**: Replace with your AWS account ID
2. **REGION**: Replace with your EKS region (us-east-1, us-west-2, etc.)
3. **OIDC Provider ID**: Replace `EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E` with your EKS cluster's OIDC provider ID

To find your OIDC provider ID:
```bash
aws eks describe-cluster --name <cluster-name> --region <region> --query 'cluster.identity.oidc.issuer' --output text
```

Example: `https://oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/ABC123DEF456...`

### ServiceAccount Configuration

The `ServiceAccount` in `infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml` is created in the `default` namespace. You may want to:
- Change the namespace to match your application deployment
- Update the subject in the OIDC trust policy to match your SA namespace/name

## Idiomatic Knr-ops Patterns Used

1. ✅ **ACK S3 & IAM CRDs**: Using s3.aws.upbound.io and iam.aws.upbound.io
2. ✅ **Kustomize Overlays**: Base + dev/prod overlays for environment differentiation
3. ✅ **namePrefix**: Applied via kustomize namePrefix for resource naming
4. ✅ **Patches**: Strategic merge patches in overlays for environment-specific values
5. ✅ **commonLabels**: Labels for resource organization and tracking
6. ✅ **Flux Kustomization Resources**: Separate reconciliation for logs stack
7. ✅ **Dependencies**: IAM resources depend on S3 resources, logs stack depends on base stacks

# Deployment Guide: Logs Stack

## Prerequisites

1. **AWS Account ID**: Required to configure OIDC trust policy
2. **EKS Cluster**: With ACK controllers installed (s3.aws.upbound.io, iam.aws.upbound.io)
3. **Flux CD**: Installed and configured with GitRepository for knr-ops
4. **kubectl**: Access to your EKS cluster

## Step 1: Configure AWS Account & OIDC

Edit `infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml` and update:

```bash
# Get your OIDC issuer URL
CLUSTER_NAME="your-cluster-name"
REGION="us-east-1"
OIDC_ID=$(aws eks describe-cluster --name $CLUSTER_NAME --region $REGION --query 'cluster.identity.oidc.issuer' --output text | cut -d '/' -f5)
ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query 'Account' --output text)

echo "ACCOUNT_ID: $ACCOUNT_ID"
echo "OIDC_ID: $OIDC_ID"
echo "REGION: $REGION"
```

Update `infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml`:
- Replace `ACCOUNT_ID` (4 occurrences)
- Replace `REGION` (2 occurrences)
- Replace `EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E` with your `OIDC_ID`

## Step 2: Configure ServiceAccount Namespace (Optional)

If deploying application to a namespace other than `default`:

```bash
# Update the ServiceAccount namespace
sed -i 's|namespace: default|namespace: your-namespace|g' infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml

# Update the OIDC subject condition
sed -i 's|system:serviceaccount:default:myapp-sa|system:serviceaccount:your-namespace:myapp-sa|g' infra/iam-logs/base/role.yaml
```

## Step 3: Test Kustomize Builds

Validate your configuration before deployment:

```bash
# Test dev environment
kustomize build overlays/dev | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -

# Test prod environment
kustomize build overlays/prod | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -

# Test logs-specific stacks
kustomize build infra/s3-logs/overlays/dev
kustomize build infra/iam-logs/overlays/dev
```

## Step 4: Deploy via Flux (Recommended)

Flux will automatically reconcile the logs stack:

```bash
# Check Flux Kustomization status
kubectl get kustomization -n flux-system | grep logs

# Watch reconciliation progress
kubectl logs -n flux-system -l app=kustomize-controller -f

# View specific Kustomization status
kubectl describe kustomization logs-dev -n flux-system
```

## Step 5: Deploy Manually (If Not Using Flux)

If Flux is not configured:

```bash
# Deploy S3 bucket
kustomize build infra/s3-logs/overlays/dev | kubectl apply -f -

# Wait for bucket creation
kubectl get bucket.s3.aws.upbound.io -w

# Deploy IAM role and ServiceAccount
kustomize build infra/iam-logs/overlays/dev | kubectl apply -f -

# Verify resources

```

```bash

kubectl get role.iam.aws.upbound.io
kubectl get rolepolicy.iam.aws.upbound.io

# Check ServiceAccount
kubectl get serviceaccount myapp-sa -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'
```
